title: Full-subcategory Kan extension restriction is a trivial Kan fibration
statement:
Use quasicategories, internal functor simplicial sets, full subcategories and coherent (co)limits of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and the fixed-endpoint arrow mapping spaces $U_X(x,y)$ of [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison]. Work in a sufficiently large fixed universe. Let $A\subseteq C$ be a full subcategory of a quasicategory, let $D$ be a quasicategory, and let $P,Q:C\to D$ be functors. For $c\in C$, the slice $C_{/c}$ consists of simplices $\Delta^n\star\Delta^0\to C$ ending at $c$, projected by the entire first face; $C_{c/}$ is its opposite convention, starting at $c$ and projected by the entire last face. Put $A_{/c}=A\times_C C_{/c}$ and $A_{c/}=A\times_C C_{c/}$. The canonical cocone or cone appends or prepends $c$.

Assume either that applying $P$ to the canonical cocone on $A_{/c}$ is colimiting for every $c$, or that applying $Q$ to the canonical cone on $A_{c/}$ is limiting for every $c$. Then the actual simplicial restriction map
$$U_{\operatorname{Fun}(C,D)}(P,Q)\longrightarrow U_{\operatorname{Fun}(A,D)}(P|_A,Q|_A)$$
is a trivial Kan fibration: for every $r\geq0$, every boundary $\partial\Delta^r$ in its source over a specified $\Delta^r$ in its target extends to that simplex exactly. In particular it is a homotopy equivalence of Kan complexes. Restriction and this equivalence are natural in the two diagrams with their coherent precomposition and postcomposition operations, including higher parameter simplices. Only the indicated local (co)limit cocones are assumed; no (co)completeness of $D$ and no extension hypothesis for every diagram on $A$ is required.

source.place: Kerodon Corollary 7.3.6.9 (030M), the actual trivial Kan fibration, via Proposition 7.3.6.7 (030F) and the relative extension argument of Proposition 7.3.5.5 (0302); no appeal to Proposition 7.3.6.1. Hom here is the fixed-endpoint arrow model. Read online; archival copy WANTED. These are Kerodon identifiers, not Stacks tags.
